nodes.description: Mapping of each account's deposited ETH; credited in the fallback and zeroed during withdrawal/refund.
Boolean flag recording whether the contract already purchased the presale tokens.
ETH value of tokens currently held by the contract; set at buy-in and decremented per withdrawal.
Maximum amount of user ETH the contract will accept (500 ether, raised to 1000 ether by upgrade_cap).
Constant minimum ETH balance (60 ether) required before the buy-in can be executed.
Address of the contract owner, set to msg.sender in the constructor; gates privileged functions.
Hard-coded crowdsale/presale address that receives the contract's ETH during buy_the_tokens.
Constructor that assigns msg.sender as the contract owner.
Any user withdraws their pro-rata share of ERC20 tokens held by the contract; reads balances, contract_eth_value and calls token.transfer.
Allows any caller to refund their deposited ETH; zeroes balance before sending ETH with msg.sender.transfer.
Owner-only buy-in: records the ETH value and forwards all funds to the sale address via a low-level call.
Owner-only function that raises eth_cap to 1000 ether.
Payable default function: accepts ETH below the cap and credits balances[msg.sender].
Caller-controlled address used as key for balances, as ETH recipient of transfers and as owner check.
require(sale.call.value(contract_eth_value)()) - unchecked low-level call forwarding all ETH to the sale address.
msg.sender.transfer(eth_to_withdraw) - external ETH transfer that hands control to the caller.
token.transfer(msg.sender, tokens_to_withdraw) - external call into an arbitrary, user-supplied ERC20 token address.
contract_eth_value -= balances[msg.sender] - arithmetic mutation of the shared stored value without underflow guard.
balances[msg.sender] += msg.value - arithmetic credit of deposited ETH, overflow-prone in Solidity 0.4.x.
this.balance + msg.value < eth_cap - arithmetic addition used for the deposit cap check.
User-supplied ERC20 token address argument of perform_withdrawal.
Recipient address parameter of the abstract ERC20.transfer declaration.
Amount parameter of the abstract ERC20.transfer declaration.
Address parameter of the abstract ERC20.balanceOf declaration.
Cached result of token.balanceOf(address(this)) inside perform_withdrawal.
Pro-rata token amount computed as (balances[msg.sender] * contract_token_balance) / contract_eth_value.
Snapshot of balances[msg.sender] taken in refund_me before the balance is cleared.
ERC20 interface instance created from the untrusted tokenAddress argument.

edges.reason: msg.sender indexes balances, whose value is subtracted from contract_eth_value.
msg.sender keys the balances mapping that is incremented by msg.value.
ETH is transferred to the caller-controlled msg.sender, giving it execution control.
refund_me executes the external ETH transfer to msg.sender.
refund_me reads balances[msg.sender] into the local eth_to_withdraw variable.
eth_to_withdraw is the value passed to msg.sender.transfer.
buy_the_tokens performs the low-level call that forwards ETH to the sale address.
The stored sale address is the target of the value-transferring low-level call.
The fallback function executes the balances[msg.sender] += msg.value update.
The fallback function evaluates the this.balance + msg.value < eth_cap cap check.
eth_cap is read as the upper bound of the deposit cap comparison.
perform_withdrawal invokes token.transfer on the externally supplied token.
perform_withdrawal stores token.balanceOf(address(this)) in contract_token_balance.
contract_token_balance is a factor of the tokens_to_withdraw computation.
contract_eth_value is the divisor of the pro-rata withdrawal computation.
contract_eth_value is the storage variable mutated by the subtraction.
The untrusted tokenAddress argument is used to instantiate the ERC20 token variable.
The ERC20 instance derived from tokenAddress is the receiver of the transfer call.
tokens_to_withdraw is passed as the amount argument of token.transfer.
owner is compared with msg.sender to gate buy_the_tokens.
owner is compared with msg.sender to gate upgrade_cap.
The constructor writes the privileged owner state variable.
buy_the_tokens sets bought_tokens to true.
buy_the_tokens records this.balance into contract_eth_value.
buy_the_tokens requires this.balance >= min_required_amount.
upgrade_cap writes the eth_cap state variable after the owner check.
msg.sender is the depositor whose balance is credited when the fallback receives ETH.
The ERC20.transfer _to parameter corresponds to the recipient of the token transfer performed by the contract.
The ERC20.transfer _value parameter corresponds to the amount argument of the token transfer.
The ERC20.balanceOf _owner parameter is the address queried by perform_withdrawal.

normalization_plan.reason: The tokenAddress parameter only exists to build the ERC20 instance used inside perform_withdrawal.
The _to parameter of the abstract ERC20.transfer is realized by the recipient argument of the external token transfer.
The _value parameter of the abstract ERC20.transfer is realized by the amount argument of the external token transfer.
The _owner parameter of the abstract ERC20.balanceOf is instantiated as address(this) inside perform_withdrawal.
Temporary cache of the token balance used only within perform_withdrawal.
Temporary pro-rata token amount consumed by the transfer inside perform_withdrawal.
Temporary ETH amount read and sent back inside refund_me.
Temporary ERC20 interface instance created from the caller-supplied token address inside perform_withdrawal.
